title: Carmakers Bank on Diwali as Maruti Bookings Climb to 2.7 Lakh After Dussehra
excerpt: Maruti Suzuki retail sales rose 35% between Ganesh Chaturthi and Dussehra with SUV sales doubling, while FADA's Navratri registrations show a more mixed industry picture distorted by a shorter festival window.
body:
• Maruti Suzuki's retail sales between Ganesh Chaturthi and Dussehra rose 35% year on year, with SUV sales doubling and small-car sales up about 16%.
  • Maruti's pending bookings climbed from about 2 lakh at the start of October to 2.7 lakh after Dussehra, and the company expects double-digit growth for the full festive period through Diwali.
  • Industry-wide passenger vehicle registrations in Navratri reached 1,82,728 units — up 10.39% on 2024 but down 21.91% on 2025, when Navratri ran 11 days against 10 this year, FADA data shows.
  • Hyundai Motor India reported registrations up about 30% to nearly 41,000 units up to Navratri, with demand healthy in both urban and rural markets.

India's carmakers are heading into Dhanteras and Diwali with full order books, after a festive season that has so far delivered a sharp rebound in showroom sales — even if the industry-wide registration numbers tell a more mixed story.

Maruti Suzuki, the country's largest passenger vehicle maker, said retail sales between Ganesh Chaturthi and Dussehra rose 35% year on year, according to reporting by Autocar Professional of the company's festive update, first reported by The Times of India. Small-car retail grew around 16%, while SUV retail doubled over the period.

"The festive season has been encouraging for Maruti Suzuki, with strong customer demand through Navratri."

— Partho Banerjee, Senior Executive Officer, Marketing and Sales, Maruti Suzuki

Order Books Are Filling Faster Than Deliveries

The clearest signal of demand is in the queue. Maruti began October with pending bookings of around 2 lakh units; after Dussehra, that figure had risen to 2.7 lakh — roughly 70,000 additional vehicles waiting for delivery. "We are making every effort to maximise deliveries and serve our customers," Banerjee said, adding that the company expects double-digit growth over the overall festive period through Diwali.

Hyundai Motor India has reported a similar pattern. Registrations up to Navratri rose about 30% year on year to nearly 41,000 units, supported by demand during Onam and Ganesh Chaturthi. "Considering the pace of bookings, we expect momentum to continue through Dhanteras and Diwali. Demand remains healthy across both urban and rural markets," said Tarun Garg, the company's MD and CEO.

Why the Industry Numbers Look Softer

Set against the company claims, the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA) registration data requires careful reading. Passenger vehicle registrations during Navratri 2026 reached 1,82,728 units — an increase of 10.39% over the 1,65,534 recorded in Navratri 2024, but a decline of 21.91% from the 2,34,004 of Navratri 2025. FADA noted that last year's Navratri covered 11 days against 10 this year, which mechanically flatters the year-earlier comparison.

Across all vehicle categories, retail registrations in Navratri stood at 11,23,086 units, up 26.76% on the comparable 2024 period. Two-wheeler registrations rose 32.41% to 8,34,075 units and commercial vehicles 16.47% to 35,618 units. The two sets of figures measure different things: FADA counts industry-wide registrations during Navratri itself, while Maruti's 35% growth covers its own retail sales over the longer Ganesh Chaturthi-to-Dussehra window.

What It Means for Buyers

For families planning a Diwali purchase — in India, and among diaspora households buying for relatives back home — the practical consequence of a 2.7 lakh-unit Maruti backlog is delivery timing: popular SUV and small-car variants booked now may not arrive before the festival. The festive offers advertised through October remain model- and dealer-specific, so the booking date and delivery slot, not the headline discount, are what buyers should lock down first. Whether the season closes with the double-digit growth Maruti expects will be clear once Dhanteras and Diwali registrations are counted in early November.
